subject: IntegrateIQ hosted ask: volume shape and budget target
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Mills <jmills@integrateiq.com>, Lee Wang <lee.wang@integrateiq.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Recap & ask: monthly tokens, peak TPS, and budget target (IntegrateIQ)

Hi Jordan / Lee —

Thanks again for the call today — good context on IntegrateIQ's planned public launch and the live-event spikes. I promised a short recap and the specific inputs we need to size a hosted pricing band and recommend a commit vs burst approach. Please reply inline if any of this is off:

Summary of your inputs (from call):
- Baseline async/chat traffic: ~45M tokens / month (production after launch).
- Average sustained TPS: ~60 requests/sec (most hours).
- Peak events: 2-3 monthly events where external traffic spikes — observed peaks up to ~2,500 TPS for roughly 8–12 minutes. These are predictable (scheduled product demos/marketing).
- Latency SLO: 600–800ms P95 for user-facing chat.
- Current target budget (internal): ~$850 per 1M tokens (asking whether we can meet or improve this in committed pricing).

Questions / missing items for pricing:
1) Are the 45M tokens/month and event spike profile (2–3 events, 8–12 min at ~2.5k TPS) the expected steady-state after GA?
2) Do you expect the bursts to be single-region or multi-region? (helps with routing/fallback planning)
3) Can you share an hourly distribution for a recent week (CSV is perfect) — that'll let us size concurrency and caching opportunities.

Proposed next steps from Redwood:
- I’ll put together two hosted pricing scenarios (committed band vs on-demand) plus an ops note on how we would absorb the 2.5k TPS spikes (routing + short burst capacity).
- I’ll attach a short pricing-matrix and a draft SLA for your legal/procurement to review.
- If the numbers look right, we can schedule a 30-min pricing review with Marissa (CC’d) and our product ops lead.

Attachments: pricing-matrix.pdf (high-level bands) — I’ll follow up with a detailed spreadsheet if you want committed math.

If that sounds right, please hit reply with: 1) confirmation of the baseline + event profile, 2) procurement contact (if different from Lee), and 3) any hard constraints on max $/1M.

Thanks — talk soon,

Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com | (415) 555-0186

From: Jordan Mills <jmills@integrateiq.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Lee Wang <lee.wang@integrateiq.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap & ask: monthly tokens, peak TPS, and budget target (IntegrateIQ)

Thanks Karthik — quick confirmation and added detail from our side.

Confirmations / clarifications:
- 45M tokens/month is our expected baseline for month-to-month production (post-launch). That includes user interactions, system prompts, and light internal QA traffic.
- Sustained load: ~60 TPS (we observe this in business hours across US users).
- Peak events: we run 2–3 orchestrated events per month that drive the 2.5k TPS peaks. They are single-region (US-east) for now and last ~8–12 minutes. We can provide the event schedule once pricing is near-final so procurement can validate burst commitments.
- Target budget: the leadership team is looking for something at or under $850 / 1M tokens for committed pricing; on-demand can be higher while we validate.

I’ve attached a small CSV with a 7-day hourly snapshot from our staging environment (IntegrateIQ_usage_snapshot.csv) that approximates the hourly shape. Note: staging underestimates a little, but the relative shape should help with batching/caching analysis.

Procurement: Lee Wang (cc’d) will be the point for contracts and budget approvals. Lee — Jordan and I will rely on your guidance for how much committed spend we can lock in this quarter.

Happy to hop on a quick pricing review later this week.

—Jordan
Jordan Mills
Head of Product | IntegrateIQ
jmills@integrateiq.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Mills <jmills@integrateiq.com>, Lee Wang <lee.wang@integrateiq.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap & ask: monthly tokens, peak TPS, and budget target (IntegrateIQ)

Appreciate the quick details — this is perfect. I reviewed the CSV and sketched two pragmatic hosted pricing scenarios that align with your budget target and burst profile. High-level (we can put exact math into a follow-up spreadsheet):

Scenario A — Committed band (recommended if you can commit):
- Commit: 50M tokens / month
- Unit price: $700 / 1M tokens (committed discount applied)
- Included burst buffer: short automated burst allowance up to 3x baseline for 10 minutes/day; beyond that bursts billed at on-demand burst rate.
- Why: locks you into a predictable $/1M below your $850 target and gives predictable monthly spend. We’ll size autoscaling to absorb the 2.5k TPS events for the 8–12 minute windows you described with pre-warmed capacity + short burst credits.

Scenario B — On-demand + short-term burst (minimal commitment):
- No monthly commit; usage billed at $1,250 / 1M tokens
- Short burst capacity available (per-minute billing) to absorb 2.5k TPS for short windows — this model is more flexible but higher unit cost while you validate production traffic.

Operational notes (how we handle the 2.5k TPS spikes):
- Single-region spikes routed to US-east with pre-warmed pools — we recommend a 30–60 minute scheduled warm-up prior to predictable events if possible to minimize cold-scaling latency.
- Prefix caching + KV-cache reuse for repeated system prompts during the event can reduce token counts by ~10–20% in practice (we'll review your prompt set).
- If the events become more frequent/longer (>30 min per event or >6 events/mo), we should consider a Dedicated capacity conversation.

Requested next inputs for the formal quote:
1) Confirm preferred scenario (A commit vs B on-demand).
2) Share any constraints from procurement on term length (monthly vs annual) and an expected start month.
3) Confirm event calendar for the next two months so we can size warm pools and list scheduled warm-ups in the SLA.

I attached the draft SLA (SLA-draft-IntegrateIQ.pdf) and the high-level pricing-matrix.pdf. If useful, Marissa can run the committed math live and walk through token-level assumptions in a 30-min call. Are you available Fri 17th or Mon 20th for a short review?

If you want, I can also hold the committed band pricing for 10 business days while you confirm internally.

Thanks — Karthik

Karthik / Marissa —

Thanks for the two scenarios. Procurement reviewed and prefers to take Scenario A (50M commit at the committed unit price) for the initial quarter, provided we can lock the $700 / 1M rate into an annual term if the launch metrics hold up. I’ve copied our legal procurement lead on the next email chain separately.

A couple of quick asks before we sign:
- Can you add a short clause in the SLA draft about short-notice burst handling for scheduled events (we will provide event dates 72+ hours in advance when possible)?
- Please confirm how overages would be billed if our bursts exceed the included burst buffer during an event.

If you can send a one-page term summary and a redline-able PO / SOW, we’ll route through contracting. Friday next week would be ideal for review, otherwise early next week.

Lee Wang
